claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can create custom user profile properties in the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: Go to More features in the new SharePoint admin center ... Under User profiles, select Open. ... Under People, select Manage User Properties. ... Select New Property.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn gives languages spoken, emergency contact info and sales account as examples of custom profile properties.
claims.quote: If you need to create custom user profile properties, such as languages spoken, emergency contact info, or sales account, you can use user properties in SharePoint.

claims.claim: These SharePoint custom profile properties are not synced back to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Note that these properties are NOT synced back to Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: The SharePoint user profile is one of the people data sources in Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The SharePoint source contains people data synchronized from the SharePoint user profile, also known as the SharePoint User Profile Application (UPA).

claims.claim: Indexed is reached in the SharePoint admin center via More features > User profiles > Open > People > Manage User Properties > New Property > Search Settings > Indexed.
claims.quote: Go to More features ... Under User profiles, select Open. ... Under People, select Manage User Properties. ... Select New Property. ... In the Search Settings section ... Select the Indexed

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The documented SharePoint Indexed setting makes searches return user profiles matching the property.
claims.quote: Select the Indexed if you want searches to return all the user profiles matching that property.

claims.claim: The custom-property instructions require an account with organizational admin permissions.
claims.quote: Go to More features in the new SharePoint admin center, and sign in with an account that has admin permissions for your organization.

claims.claim: Property privacy controls are in the SharePoint admin center via More features > User profiles > Open > People > Manage User Properties > New Property > Policy Settings.
claims.quote: Under User profiles, select Open. ... Under People, select Manage User Properties. ... Select New Property. ... In the Policy Settings section, select the policy setting and default privacy setting that you want for this property.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Each custom property has a configurable default privacy setting in Policy Settings.
claims.quote: In the Policy Settings section, select the policy setting and default privacy setting that you want for this property.

claims.claim: The User can override box permits users to override a property's policy and privacy settings.
claims.quote: Select the User can override box to enable users to override these settings.

claims.claim: A property has an Allow users to edit values for this property setting.
claims.quote: If you want users to be able to change this profile information for themselves, select Allow users to edit values for this property.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, inventory bullet
claims.claim: The inventory route is SharePoint admin center > More features > User profiles > Manage User Properties.
claims.quote: Select User profiles, and then select Open. Under People, choose Manage User Properties.
claims.fix: Replace the inventory bullet's path with 'More features > User profiles > Open > People > Manage User Properties' in the SharePoint admin center, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/add-and-edit-user-profile-properties. Open is a required labeled selection, not an omitted heading.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, edit/delete bullet
claims.claim: Custom properties can be edited or deleted from Manage User Properties.
claims.quote: Under People, choose Manage User Properties. ... In the Property Name column, select the profile property that you want to change, and then select Edit or Delete.

claims.claim: Learn's bulk-update page states that no remote API creates custom user profile properties.
claims.quote: Because there are no remote APIs for creating custom properties in the user profile service, this step must be performed manually for each of the tenants where custom user profile properties are needed

claims.claim: The CSOM method QueueImportProfileProperties queues a bulk import of user profile property values.
claims.quote: You can queue the CSOM API for the bulk import process by calling the QueueImportProfileProperties method located in the Office365Tenant object.

claims.claim: The bulk import works only for properties not configured to be editable by end users.
claims.quote: The import only works for user profile properties that have not been set to be editable by end users.

claims.claim: The bulk import requires Global Admin permissions unless an app-only authentication context is used.
claims.quote: You must have Global Admin permissions currently, unless you use an app-only authentication context. SharePoint Admin is not sufficient.

claims.claim: The general Copilot Search admin experience is reached via Copilot > Search in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center: ... From the left navigation menu, select Copilot from the dropdown menu and select Search.

claims.claim: The general Copilot Search admin experience supports managing bookmarks, acronyms and connectors.
claims.quote: For example, you can manage connectors, bookmarks, and acronyms for Copilot Search just as you can for Microsoft Search.

claims.claim: The managing-user-profiles article is written for SharePoint Administrators and above.
claims.quote: This article is for SharePoint Administrators and above in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The general Copilot Search FAQ states that Copilot returns only information the user already has access to.
claims.quote: Copilot only returns information that the user already has access to-respecting existing permissions and security boundaries.
